review_notes: Source-first scope check: the principal empirical tests assess the reporting-bias predictions with portfolio analyses (Tables 3–4) and reversal-portfolio comparisons of subsequent returns (Tables 5–7), rather than a baseline regression family. Equation (3) is an actual cross-sectional risk-adjustment regression used to construct abnormal-return outcomes for those portfolios; it does not itself test the principal hypotheses. Endnote 19 reporting-bias regressions and endnote 20 monthly-return regressions are supplementary checks, not replacements for the principal portfolio designs. The no_baseline_regression status means no principal baseline regression is retained; it does not mean the paper contains no regressions.
descriptive_reason: No baseline regression is retained for this paper, so there are no retained model variables for related descriptive statistics.
results_review_notes: Confirmed the frozen no_baseline_regression scope: the principal tests are portfolio comparisons in Tables 3–4 (physical PDF pages 16–22) and reversal portfolios in Tables 5–7 (pages 26–40). The table headers and notes describe yearly formed portfolios, their means/medians and Fama–MacBeth statistics; they are not baseline regression result sets.

Equation (3) on page 23 is a cross-sectional return-risk regression used to create abnormal-return residuals reported in portfolio analyses. Endnote 19 (pages 47–48) describes reporting-bias regressions and endnote 20 describes monthly-return regressions; both are supplemental checks and not substitutes for the principal portfolio designs. No baseline model or model-linked descriptive rows are therefore added.
